Gemini Notebook Enterprise is a powerful tool for generating insights and
summaries from your documents. This page describes the APIs that let you
perform the following notebook management tasks programmatically:

* Create a notebook
* Retrieve a notebook
* List recently viewed notebooks
* Delete a notebook
* Share a notebook

## Before you begin

Before you start working with your notebooks, do the following:

* [Set up Gemini Notebook Enterprise](docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-notebooklm) .
* [Get licenses for Gemini Notebook Enterprise](docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-licensing) and assign a license to your user account.
* [Grant the Cloud NotebookLM User role](docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-notebooklm) ( `roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmUser` ) to your user account.
* In a local terminal or [Cloud Shell](docs.cloud.google.com/shell/docs) , sign in to the [Google Cloud CLI](docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk) with your user credentials by running
  the [`gcloud auth login`](docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/auth/login) command:
  
  ```
  gcloud auth login
  ```
  
  Signing in with your user credentials ensures that `gcloud auth print-access-token` generates an access token for your user
  account. The [`projects.locations.notebooks` REST API](docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rest/v1alpha/projects.locations.notebooks) methods on
  this page require an authenticated user account with an active
  Gemini Notebook Enterprise license.

...

## README.md

Note

**This is a maintained fork** of [`PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp`](github.com/PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp) , which was archived in September 2026. The fork keeps the server working after NotebookLM was rebranded **Gemini Notebook** and moved to `notebook.google.com` .

The `notebooklm-mcp` package on npm is the **archived upstream release** and does not include these fixes. Until this fork is published under its own name (see Roadmap ), install it from source .

# NotebookLM MCP Server

[TypeScript](typescriptlang.org/) [MCP](modelcontextprotocol.io/) [License](github.com/MatiNovelli/notebooklm-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE)

MCP server for Google NotebookLM, now **Gemini Notebook** ( `notebook.google.com` ; the legacy `notebooklm.google.com` host still works). There is no official API, so it drives a real Chrome via Patchright (stealth + persistent fingerprint) so an agent can chat against a notebook, ingest sources, generate audio overviews, and read DOM-level citations. Two transports are supported: `stdio` (default) and Streamable-HTTP. v2.0.0 is the current line; v1 is no longer supported.

Because it reads answers from the live web UI, it can break whenever Google changes that UI.

* Requirements
* Install
* Connect — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, generic MCP
* Authentication
* Transports
* Multi-account
* Tools
* Profiles
* Citations
* Provenance & AI marker
* Configuration reference
* Development
* Known issues
* Roadmap
* Migration from v1

...

## Requirements & Platform Support

* **Node.js** ≥ 18.
* **Chrome** (stable channel) preferred. The bundled Patchright Chromium is used as a fallback when Chrome refuses to launch — set `BROWSER_CHANNEL=chromium` to force it.
* **Linux / macOS / Windows.**
* **WSL2 + WSLg** (Windows 11+) is fully supported. WSL1 cannot launch a Chromium and is not supported — upgrade to WSL2.
* **Headless Linux servers** : the one-time `setup_auth` needs a display because the login flow opens a visible window. Run it once under `xvfb-run` ( `xvfb-run -a notebooklm-mcp` ). After login, the persistent Chrome profile lets every subsequent run go fully headless.

* * *

## Install

Important

Do not use `notebooklm-mcp` : it downloads the archived upstream release, which fails on `notebook.google.com` .

...

### Codex CLI

```shell
codex mcp add notebooklm notebooklm-mcp
```

### Generic MCP client (stdio)

Any client that can spawn an MCP server over stdio can use the same `notebooklm-mcp` command (or `node /absolute/path/to/dist/index.js` ). The server speaks MCP 2025 + the SDK's `Server` capability set ( `tools` , `resources` , `prompts` , `completions` , `logging` ).

### HTTP-only clients (n8n, Zapier, Make, hosted agents)

Run the server in HTTP mode (see Transports ) and POST JSON-RPC against `host:port/mcp` . A short curl example lives in [`docs/usage-guide.md`](github.com/MatiNovelli/notebooklm-mcp/blob/main/docs/usage-guide.md) .

* * *

## Authentication

`setup_auth` opens a visible Chrome, you log in to your Google account once, and the cookies are persisted in the per-user Chrome profile. Subsequent runs reuse that profile and do not need to log in again.

...

### stdio (default)

```shell
notebooklm-mcp
```

## REST API server

> **⚠️ Experimental.** Like the MCP adapter, the REST server is experimental: the `/v1` surface and behavior may change in a minor release, and it is excluded from the public-API compatibility gate. Pin a version before relying on it for automation. The server also logs an experimental warning on every startup.

A local-first REST API over the same transport-neutral core as the CLI — the natural shape for scripting and agent automation (feed a notebook, generate an artifact, pull it down) without spawning a CLI process per call.

The [REST subsystem diagram](teng-lin.github.io/notebooklm-py/diagrams/18-rest-server-subsystem.html) shows its
lifespan-owned client, route guards, concurrency limits, and response projection.

...

**Launch:**

```bash
export NOTEBOOKLM_SERVER_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"   # REQUIRED — the server refuses to start without it
notebooklm-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000            # loopback-only by default
```

...

### Android multi-profile MCP

MCP can serve several already-provisioned Android profiles over either stdio or HTTP:

```bash
uv tool install --force "notebooklm-py[mcp,android]"
notebooklm-mcp --backend android --profiles work,personal
# Or set NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_PROFILES=work,personal and NOTEBOOKLM_BACKEND=android.
# Add --transport http to use the existing HTTP authentication and bind settings.
```

...

`NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_PROFILE_STARTUP_TIMEOUT` configures the positive,
finite per-attempt deadline (default: 30 seconds, including the readiness read).
Expired attempts cannot publish a client; retries wait for their cancellation
cleanup to settle, and shutdown drains owned tasks after cancelling detached chats.
`server_info(profile=...)` reports Android credential health and readiness without
probing Web credentials.

Signed upload/download URLs bind the issuing profile. Upload receipt polling and
widget confirmation use that same profile. The HTTP bearer or OAuth credential
authorizes **all** configured profiles; selection is routing, not per-account
access control. Existing HTTP bind and authentication requirements still apply.

### Web multi-profile MCP

The default Web backend serves several profiles the same way:

```bash
notebooklm-mcp --profiles work,personal
# Or set NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_PROFILES=work,personal (NOTEBOOKLM_BACKEND unset or web).
```

...

Profile
opens take turns in the background, so `initialize` and tool discovery never wait
for them, and the wait does not count against the startup timeout. A first or
recovering tool call for a profile can wait behind other profiles' queued attempts.
`server_info(profile=...)` reports `backend: "web"` with the same file-only health
fields as REST, including `session_conflict`.

### Running the MCP server (`mcp` extra)

The MCP server ships behind the optional `mcp` extra (see the extras matrix above) and exposes the same `_app/` business logic over the Model Context Protocol.

```bash
notebooklm-mcp                                         # installed console script (stdio transport)
uvx --from "notebooklm-py[mcp]" notebooklm-mcp         # no install — run straight from PyPI
```

excerpts:
Google documents using @Gemini Notebook in a chat or task thread. If a connection is needed, Gemini offers the connection flow; it can also be managed in Connected Apps settings. Documented actions include listing notebooks, answering questions, managing sources and creating, editing or deleting notebooks. Availability is still rolling out. Google’s connection guide
For ordinary notebook work within Gemini, this is the first path to investigate. The cited guide does not document a public MCP endpoint or an mcpServers setting. Its supported actions also include writes and deletion, so “official” does not mean “read-only.”
For source-analysis prompts after choosing your connection, see our Gemini Notebook templates .

The community MCP option: identify the actual package

We examined jacob-bd/gemini-notebook-mcp-cli , an unofficial project whose package and executable names retain “NotebookLM.” Its code targets the notebook web service, including notebook, source and chat operations.

...

In the reviewed implementation, nlm login uses a managed browser to obtain Google session cookies. It is not a Gemini API-key login or an OAuth flow with narrowly selected Notebook scopes. nlm login --check validates credentials against the service; it is not an offline syntax check. Authentication documentation
The project supports file-based and protected credential storage. Protected storage depends on the operating system’s keyring facilities, so it should not be assumed to work in a headless SSH environment. The connector’s requests use internal web RPC endpoints, including a separate enterprise web route. Those routes are different from Google’s documented Enterprise REST API. Storage configuration , request routing

Default tools include changes and sharing

...

The official Enterprise API is a separate path

Google documents a Preview API for creating and managing enterprise notebooks. It uses Discovery Engine REST resources under a project and location, with OAuth authorization and Enterprise setup and access requirements. This is a relevant starting point for organizations that need an official integration. It does not establish equivalent API access for a personal notebook account, and it is not itself an MCP server. results.title: NotebookLM MCP: install, tools and limits
excerpts:
By Better Design
Published: 2026-11-12
<A hand-drawn terminal that connects a coding agent to NotebookLM MCP, with the server's name and tool count written beside it.>
NotebookLM MCP is Google's official remote MCP server for Gemini Notebook, the new name for NotebookLM, and it lets a coding agent create and list notebooks and add sources to them. It runs over Streamable HTTP at notebook.googleapis.com/mcp, needs a Google OAuth access token, and exposes 7 tools.

What NotebookLM MCP does

NotebookLM MCP is Google's official remote MCP server for Gemini Notebook, the new name for NotebookLM, and it lets a coding agent create and list notebooks and add sources to them. It is in Public Preview and mirrors the 7 methods of the Gemini Notebook REST API.
Google maintains it.

How a coding agent uses NotebookLM MCP

...

export PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
gcloud services enable notebook.googleapis.com --project="$PROJECT_ID"
gcloud auth application-default login --scopes="googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook"
export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)
claude mcp add gemini-notebook-api --transport http notebook.googleapis.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --header "x-goog-user-project: $PROJECT_ID"

Install NotebookLM MCP in Cursor

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gemini-notebook-api": {
      "url": "notebook.googleapis.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN",
        "x-goog-user-project": "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
      }
    }
  }
}

The 7 tools NotebookLM MCP gives your agent

NotebookLM MCP lists these names in its own documentation, read on November 12, 2026. Your agent sees each one as a tool it can call.
* create_notebook
* get_notebook
* list_notebooks
* update_notebook
* create_source
* get_source
* list_sources

Settings worth knowing in NotebookLM MCP

Documented NotebookLM MCP settings
* Setting | What it changes | Server
* list_notebooks filter notebook.is_owner = true or false | Lists only the notebooks you own, or only the ones shared with you. | NotebookLM MCP
* create_source webContent.url or textContent | Adds a web page or YouTube URL, or inline text with mimeType text/markdown. | NotebookLM MCP
* get_source state | Returns the processing state: PROCESSING, ACTIVE or FAILED. | NotebookLM MCP
* googleapis.com/auth/notebook.readonly | A read-only scope for the get and list tools. | NotebookLM MCP

Sign-in, limits and caveats for NotebookLM MCP

Sign-in: An OAuth 2.0 Bearer token with the scope googleapis.com/auth/notebook (or notebook.readonly), plus the header x-goog-user-project for Application Default Credentials. It takes no API keys. During the preview only personal Google Accounts work; Workspace accounts get 403 WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT_NOT_SUPPORTED. The account must have signed in to Gemini Notebook once.
Limits and price: Free during the Public Preview. Per project: 100 read and 100 write requests per minute. Per user: 20 CreateSource requests per minute and 60 per minute for each other method. Each source holds up to 500,000 words and 1 MB of inline text. Notebooks per user and sources per notebook depend on the tier: Free 100 and 50, Plus 200 and 100, Pro 500 and 300, Ultra 500 and 600.
* It cannot query a notebook or generate artifacts such as Audio Overviews yet. Google's roadmap lists both, with Workspace accounts, binary uploads, deletes and Drive sources.

...

results.title: MCP server guide
excerpts:
# MCP server guide

**Last Updated:** 2026-09-29

> **Experimental / preview.** The MCP server ships behind the optional `mcp` extra. Its
> tool surface (names, parameters, output shapes) is **not** covered by the library's semver
> guarantees and may change between releases. `pip install notebooklm-py` is unaffected — the
> server and its dependencies only arrive with the `mcp` extra.

The MCP server exposes NotebookLM to any [Model Context Protocol](modelcontextprotocol.io)
client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, …) as a set of **38 tools** — manage
notebooks and sources, chat over a notebook's sources, generate and download studio artifacts,
and run deep research. It is a thin adapter over the same business logic the CLI uses, so it
behaves identically to `notebooklm <command>`.

See the [MCP subsystem diagram](teng-lin.github.io/notebooklm-py/diagrams/17-mcp-subsystem.html) for process and
application boundaries. Remote file movement is expanded in the
[transfer-security data flow](teng-lin.github.io/notebooklm-py/diagrams/30-transfer-security-boundaries.dataflow.html).
The operator-facing hosting threat model is [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).

## Install

The server is behind the `mcp` extra (pulls in `fastmcp`):

```bash
pip install "notebooklm-py[mcp]"
# or run with no install, straight from PyPI:
uvx --from "notebooklm-py[mcp]" notebooklm-mcp --help
```

## Authenticate (once)

The server reuses a stored profile — it does **not** log in on its own. For the
default Web backend, authenticate once before starting it:

```bash
notebooklm login
# or, if you didn't install the package:
uvx --from "notebooklm-py[mcp]" notebooklm login
```

Credentials are stored per profile under `~/.notebooklm/`. The server binds the **active profile**
at startup (override with `--profile`, below). See [configuration.md](configuration.md) for profiles
and multi-account setup.

For `--backend android`, include Android plus the browser needed for the one-time
interactive bootstrap, then initialize the same profile the server will bind:

```bash
pip install "notebooklm-py[mcp,android,browser]"
notebooklm --profile work login --master-token --account you@example.com
notebooklm-mcp --profile work --backend android
```

...

## Connect a client

The fastest path is the auto-config command, which writes the server block into a client's MCP
config (idempotent, never clobbers other servers):

```bash
notebooklm mcp install claude-desktop   # or: claude-code | cursor | windsurf
```

...

## Run it directly

The console script is `notebooklm-mcp`:

```bash
notebooklm-mcp                         # stdio transport (default — for desktop hosts)
notebooklm-mcp --profile work          # bind a specific auth profile
notebooklm-mcp --backend android        # Android adapters; requires Android auth setup
notebooklm-mcp --transport http        # loopback streamable-HTTP on 127.0.0.1:9420
notebooklm-mcp --transport http --port 9000
```

| Flag | Default | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| `--profile` | active profile | which stored auth profile the process binds |
| `--backend` | `web` | `web` or `android`; overrides `NOTEBOOKLM_BACKEND` |
| `--transport` | `stdio` | `stdio` (subprocess hosts) or `http` (loopback) |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | http only; non-loopback is **refused** unless `NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_BIND=1` |
| `--port` | `9420` | http only |
| `--log-level` | `INFO` | logs go to **stderr**; stdout stays pure JSON-RPC |

There is no `--token` flag — the HTTP bearer token is **env-only**
(`NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_TOKEN`) so it cannot leak via `ps aux`.

...

**Two auth methods coexist on one `/mcp`** (FastMCP `MultiAuth`):
- **Claude Code / Desktop** → the static `NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_TOKEN` bearer (an `Authorization` header).
- **claude.ai (web/mobile) and ChatGPT** (Developer Mode) → optional **self-hosted OAuth** (one
  password, no external IdP): set `NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_OAUTH_PASSWORD` (≥16 random chars) +
  `NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_OAUTH_BASE_URL` (the **bare public origin**, no `/mcp`). Both connector UIs are
  OAuth-only (no bearer field). Unset → bearer-only (Claude Code/Desktop still work).

Use a **dedicated/throwaway Google account** — the mounted `master_token.json` is a durable
full-account credential. Multi-tenant hosting is out of scope for this single-tenant setup.

# Create and manage notebooks (API) Stay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences.



Gemini Notebook Enterprise is a powerful tool for generating insights and
summaries from your documents. This page describes the APIs that let you
perform the following notebook management tasks programmatically:

## Before you begin

Before you start working with your notebooks, do the following:

* Set up Gemini Notebook Enterprise.
* Get licenses for Gemini Notebook Enterprise
  and assign a license to your user account.
* Grant the Cloud NotebookLM User role
  (`roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmUser`) to your user account.
* In a local terminal or Cloud Shell, sign in to the
  Google Cloud CLI with your user credentials by running
  the `gcloud auth login` command:

  ```
  gcloud auth login
  ```

  Signing in with your user credentials ensures that
  `gcloud auth print-access-token` generates an access token for your user
  account. The `projects.locations.notebooks` REST
  API methods on
  this page require an authenticated user account with an active
  Gemini Notebook Enterprise license.

## Use the US multi-regional endpoint

If your Gemini Notebook Enterprise subscription is in the US
multi-region, you can send the requests on this page to the US multi-regional
endpoint, `discoveryengine.us.rep.googleapis.com`. A multi-regional endpoint
processes your requests and terminates TLS within the multi-region, so your
request data stays in the US while it's in transit. Using this endpoint doesn't
change where your notebooks are stored. For more information, see
Regional and multi-regional API endpoints
overview in the Google Cloud
security guide.

To use the US multi-regional endpoint, make the following changes to each
request URL on this page:

1. Replace the
   `ENDPOINT_LOCATION-discoveryengine.googleapis.com`
   host with `discoveryengine.us.rep.googleapis.com`.
2. Set `LOCATION` to `us`.

The rest of each request stays the same. To learn how you choose your
subscription's multi-region, see
Get a subscription.
For the list of regional and multi-regional service endpoints, see
Regional and multi-regional service endpoints
in the Virtual Private Cloud guide.

## Create a notebook

To create a new notebook, use the
`notebooks.create`
method.

### REST

```
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization:Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://ENDPOINT_LOCATION-discoveryengine.googleapis.com/v1alpha/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION/notebooks" \
  -d '{
  "title": "NOTEBOOK_TITLE",
  }'
```

Replace the following:

* `ENDPOINT_LOCATION`: the multi-region for your API request. Specify one of the following
  values:
  + `us` for the US multi-region
  + `eu` for the EU multi-region
  + `global` for the Global locationFor more information, see
  Specify a multi-region
  for your data store.
* `PROJECT_NUMBER`: the number of your Google Cloud project.
* `LOCATION`:
  the geographic location of your data store, such as `global`.
  For more information, see Locations.
* `NOT

   management tasks, such as sharing.

## Retrieve a notebook

To retrieve a specific notebook using its notebook ID, use the
`notebooks.get`
method.

### REST

```

  -H "Authorization:Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \

# Model Context Protocol (MCP) Stay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences.



The Gemini Notebook API provides a remote **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**
server at `https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp`. Connecting an MCP-compatible
agent or IDE to this endpoint exposes tools for creating notebooks and
ingesting sources over Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0).

## Quickstart prompt for coding agents (Recommended)

Click **Show prompt**, copy the prompt, and paste it into your coding agent
(such as Claude Code or Cursor) to automate Google Cloud setup,
OAuth token generation, and MCP server configuration:

```
Help me connect to the remote Gemini Notebook MCP server (`https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp`). Follow these exact steps:

1. Check if `gcloud` is installed and ask me which Google Cloud PROJECT_ID to use (you can list my projects with `gcloud projects list --limit=10` or check `gcloud config get-value project`).
2. Enable the Gemini Notebook API on that project:
   gcloud services enable notebook.googleapis.com --project="$PROJECT_ID"
3. Authenticate Application Default Credentials (ADC) with a personal Google Account (Google Workspace accounts are not yet supported) that has signed in to https://notebook.google.com at least once, requesting the `notebook` OAuth scope (standard `gcloud auth print-access-token` lacks this scope):
   gcloud auth application-default login --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook"
4. Mint an access token:
   ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)
